title: Conclusion Engine
boundary: Conclusions are evidence-bounded editorial outputs. They must not turn speculation, association or source proximity into proof.

conclusions.title: Mission conclusion engine
conclusions.conclusion: The site should treat every page as part of one intelligence loop: collect source, classify it, grade evidence, connect it to the map, publish a bounded conclusion, then review it when new records arrive.
conclusions.why: This turns the site from an archive into a living research machine.
conclusions.boundary: This is an editorial workflow, not proof that any mapped actor has secret intent or wrongdoing.
conclusions.next: Use information-gathering-system.html as the operating manual and conclusion-engine.html as the reader-facing output route.

conclusions.title: Current strongest public signal
conclusions.conclusion: Surveillance State Clock is currently the strongest pressure signal at 92/100.
conclusions.why: The strongest clock should drive today’s brief, card routing and missing-record hunt.
conclusions.boundary: Clock score is a speculative pressure score, not prediction or certainty.
conclusions.next: Open timers.html and follow the linked latestDrops before making stronger claims.

conclusions.title: Best source intake priority
conclusions.conclusion: The highest-priority source drop is EU AI Act implementation enters 2026 enforcement phase with transparency rules due August 2026 and high-risk timelines clarified.
conclusions.why: Fresh dated source drops are the cleanest way to keep clocks, cards and briefs current.
conclusions.boundary: A source drop is a lead until it has been classified, cross-checked and connected to a conclusion.
conclusions.next: Route the source into the relevant clock, card, policy lane and missing-record queue.

conclusions.title: Card system conclusion
conclusions.conclusion: The card layer currently reports 9 decks and 468 feed cards in the intelligence feed.
conclusions.why: Decks are the visual navigation layer; dossiers and ledgers are where evidence and updates live.
conclusions.boundary: Card inclusion is research relevance, not accusation.
conclusions.next: Use the source ledger and card forum to add reviewed source-backed notes card by card.

conclusions.title: Information gathering gap
conclusions.conclusion: The site needs reader submissions to be treated as leads, not claims: each submission should capture URL, source type, what it shows, what it does not show, deck/card route, correction status and review decision.
conclusions.why: This prevents the forum/intake areas from becoming rumour dumps and makes them useful for research.
conclusions.boundary: User submissions are unreviewed until checked.
conclusions.next: Push all intake areas toward the same evidence-slot standard.

topDrops.laneTitle: AI Governance / EU AI Act / Cybersecurity
topDrops.sourceLabel: European Commission AI Act page, last updated 2026-07-07
topDrops.title: EU AI Act implementation enters 2026 enforcement phase with transparency rules due August 2026 and high-risk timelines clarified
topDrops.summary: The Commission's AI Act page now frames the AI Act as an active implementation file: prohibited practices applied from February 2025, GPAI rules from August 2025, transparency rules from August 2026, and high-risk obligations staged through December 2027 and August 2028 after simplification/political agreement language.
topDrops.evidenceLevel: Official EU implementation timeline / regulatory governance lane
topDrops.evidenceBoundary: Implementation dates and obligations are not proof of censorship or abuse. Track the legal text, guidance, enforcement actions, standards, national authorities, and actual platform behaviour separately.
topDrops.whyItMatters: This is now a live AI governance clock, not a future theory. It connects model providers, transparency duties, cybersecurity, national authorities, and high-risk public-sector/biometric/migration systems.
topDrops.nextAction: Update AI Breakout, Surveillance State and Machine Convergence clocks; watch August 2026 transparency duties, 2027 high-risk application, AI Office guidance, and enforcement cases.
topDrops.sourceRequirement: Official Commission AI Act page, EU legal text, AI Office guidance, national authority page, enforcement decision, or official standardisation document

topDrops.laneTitle: WHO Pandemic Agreement / PABS / Global Health Governance
topDrops.sourceLabel: WHO Pandemic Agreement page and July 2026 IGWG listing
topDrops.title: WHO Pandemic Agreement remains adopted but not fully open for ratification until PABS annex is negotiated
topDrops.summary: WHO states the Pandemic Agreement was adopted on 20 May 2025, but the next step is negotiation of the Pathogen Access and Benefit-Sharing system as an annex. WHO lists the seventh IGWG meeting on the Agreement for 6–17 July 2026.
topDrops.evidenceBoundary: Treaty adoption is not the same as force, ratification, domestic implementation, or WHO control over national measures. WHO states the agreement does not authorize it to impose lockdowns or vaccine mandates.
topDrops.whyItMatters: This is the current biosecurity governance lane: PABS, pathogen sharing, supply-chain/logistics network, finance mechanism, national ratification, and domestic implementation plans.
topDrops.nextAction: Update Pandemic/Biosecurity and Surveillance State clocks; watch IGWG outputs, PABS annex text, ratification counts, national legislation, and financing mechanisms.
topDrops.sourceRequirement: WHO agreement text, WHA decision, IGWG document, PABS annex draft, national ratification record, or official parliamentary record

topDrops.laneTitle: Digital ID / EUDI Wallet / Credential Disclosure
topDrops.sourceLabel: EUDI Wallet regulation timeline plus June 2026 credential-disclosure study
topDrops.title: EUDI Wallet remains a late-2026 implementation watch, with new research warning about user oversharing risks
topDrops.summary: A June 2026 study on EUDI Wallet-style credential disclosure warns that users may overshare sensitive credentials, including official ID attributes, and that assistant-style mitigations reduce but do not eliminate disclosure mistakes.
topDrops.evidenceLevel: Academic implementation-risk study / digital identity rollout lane
topDrops.evidenceBoundary: A usability/privacy study is not proof of deliberate abuse. Track national wallet launches, relying-party rules, disclosure UX, audits, regulator actions, and real incidents separately.
topDrops.whyItMatters: Digital ID risk is moving from abstract policy to wallet UX, relying-party access, credential disclosure, and whether the user can meaningfully control what is shared.
topDrops.nextAction: Update Surveillance State, CBDC Rollout and Machine Convergence clocks; watch late-2026 national wallet availability, relying-party registries, private-sector acceptance, and credential-sharing defaults.
topDrops.sourceRequirement: EUDI regulation, implementing act, national wallet documentation, relying-party registry, privacy audit, or peer-reviewed/academic study

topDrops.laneTitle: CBDC / Digital Euro / Sovereign Payment Rails
topDrops.title: ECB says digital euro aims for potential first issuance during 2029 if EU legislation is adopted in 2026
topDrops.summary: The ECB states the Eurosystem moved to the next phase of the digital euro project in October 2025 and aims to be ready for potential first issuance during 2029, assuming EU legislation is adopted during 2026. The ECB frames the digital euro as a central-bank digital form of cash complementing banknotes and coins.
topDrops.evidenceLevel: Official ECB CBDC project timeline / legislation and technical-readiness lane
topDrops.evidenceBoundary: A readiness target is not a final launch. Track legislation, pilots, wallet design, holding limits, privacy design, bank costs, merchant rules, and adoption requirements separately.
topDrops.whyItMatters: The money-rails clock is now tied to legislative timing, technical readiness, euro-area payment sovereignty, online/offline design, and the relationship between digital public money and existing private payment systems.
topDrops.nextAction: Update CBDC Rollout and Financial Reset clocks; watch 2026 legislative adoption, 2027 testing, wallet provider rules, privacy architecture, and 2029 issuance decision.
topDrops.sourceRequirement: ECB project page, ECB progress report, EU legislative text, Parliament/Council record, pilot documentation, or official privacy/holding-limit design
